Shortcut Trick

Apply Mode formula: L + [(f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)] × h

L = 25, f₁ = 11, f₀ = 9, f₂ = 10, h = 5

Mode = 25 + [(11 − 9) ÷ (22 − 9 − 10)] × 5 = 25 + (2 ÷ 3) × 5 = 25 + 3.33

Mode = L + [ (f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) ] × h

⇒ Mode = 25 + [ 2 ÷ 3 ] × 5

⇒ Mode = 25 + 10 ÷ 3

⇒ Mode = 25 + 3.333...

⇒ Mode ≈ 28.33

∴ The correct answer is 28.33.

q:
The arithmetic mean of the following data is _.

23, 17, 20, 19, 21
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Assume a base value for the mean, say 20.

Find deviations from 20: (23 − 20) = +3, (17 − 20) = −3, (20 − 20) = 0, (19 − 20) = −1, (21 − 20) = +1.

Sum of deviations = 3 − 3 + 0 − 1 + 1 = 0.

Arithmetic Mean = Base + (Total Deviation ÷ Count) = 20 + (0 ÷ 5) = 20.

∴ The correct answer is 20.

Alternate Method

Given:

Data values: 23, 17, 20, 19, 21

Total number of observations (n) = 5

Formula Used:

Arithmetic Mean (χ) = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)



Calculations:

⇒ Sum = 23 + 17 + 20 + 19 + 21

⇒ Sum = 100

⇒ Mean = 100 ÷ 5

⇒ Mean = 20

∴ The correct answer is 20.

Additional Information

Arithmetic Mean Properties

The sum of deviations of a set of observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero. If each observation is increased by a constant k, the mean also increases by k.

Range of Data

Range is the difference between the maximum and minimum values in a data set. For this data: Range = 23 − 17 = 6.

Median

The median is the middle value when the data is arranged in ascending or descending order. For 17, 19, 20, 21, 23, the median is 20.

q:
The median of the following data will be _.

32, 25, 33, 27, 35, 29 and 30
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Arrange the data in ascending order: 25, 27, 29, 30, 32, 33, 35.

The number of terms (n) = 7, which is an odd number.

For an odd number of terms, the median is the middle-most value.

The middle term is the 4th term in the sorted list.

The 4th term is 30.

∴ The correct answer is 30.

Alternate Method

Given: Data set = {32, 25, 33, 27, 35, 29, 30}

Formula Used: Median = [(n + 1) / 2]th term, where n is the number of observations (when n is odd).



⇒ Count the number of observations in the data set:

⇒ n = 7 (which is odd)

⇒ Arrange the data in ascending order: 25, 27, 29, 30, 32, 33, 35

⇒ Median = [(7 + 1) / 2]th observation

⇒ Median = 8 / 2 = 4th observation

⇒ The 4th observation in the sorted list is 30.

∴ The correct answer is 30.

Additional Information

Median for Even n

When the number of observations (n) is even, the median is calculated as the average of the (n/2)th and (n/2 + 1)th terms.

Importance of Sorting

The data must always be arranged in either ascending or descending order before identifying the middle term; otherwise, the result will be incorrect.

Range of Data

The range is the difference between the maximum and minimum values: Range = Max − Min. For this data, Range = 35 − 25 = 10.

q:
Find the standard deviation of the following data (rounded off to two decimal places).

5, 3, 4, 7
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Mean (μ) = (5 + 3 + 4 + 7) ÷ 4 = 19 ÷ 4 = 4.75

Sum of squares (Σx²) = 5² + 3² + 4² + 7² = 25 + 9 + 16 + 49 = 99

Standard Deviation (σ) = √[(Σx² ÷ n) − μ²]

σ = √[(99 ÷ 4) − 4.75²] = √[24.75 − 22.5625] = √2.1875 ≈ 1.48

∴ The correct answer is 1.48.

Alternate Method

Given: Data points = {5, 3, 4, 7}, Number of observations (n) = 4

Formula Used: σ = √[Σ(xᵢ − μ)² ÷ n]



⇒ Mean (μ) = (5 + 3 + 4 + 7) ÷ 4 = 4.75

⇒ Squared deviation for 5: (5 − 4.75)² = 0.25² = 0.0625

⇒ Squared deviation for 3: (3 − 4.75)² = (−1.75)² = 3.0625

⇒ Squared deviation for 4: (4 − 4.75)² = (−0.75)² = 0.5625

⇒ Squared deviation for 7: (7 − 4.75)² = 2.25² = 5.0625

⇒ Variance (σ²) = (0.0625 + 3.0625 + 0.5625 + 5.0625) ÷ 4 = 8.75 ÷ 4 = 2.1875

⇒ Standard Deviation (σ) = √2.1875 ≈ 1.48

∴ The correct answer is 1.48.

Additional Information

Variance

Variance is the average of the squared differences from the mean, calculated as σ² = Σ(x − μ)² ÷ n.

Coefficient of Variation (CV)

It is a relative measure of dispersion calculated as CV = (σ ÷ μ) × 100%.

Range

Range is the simplest measure of dispersion, defined as the difference between the maximum and minimum values in a dataset.

q: For a sample data, mean = 60 and median = 48. For this distribution, the mode is:
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Direct Empirical Formula: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

Substitute: Mode = 3(48) − 2(60)

Calculate: 144 − 120 = 24

∴ The correct answer is 24.

Alternate Method

Given:

Mean = 60

Median = 48

Formula Used:

For a moderately skewed distribution, the empirical relation is:

Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean



Calculations:

⇒ Mode = 3 × 48 − 2 × 60

⇒ Mode = 144 − 120

⇒ Mode = 24

∴ The correct answer is 24.

Additional Information

Empirical Relation (Karl Pearson)

The relationship Mean − Mode = 3 × (Mean − Median) is used for moderately skewed asymmetrical distributions.

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly symmetrical distribution, the Mean, Median, and Mode are all equal (Mean = Median = Mode).

Skewness Identification

When Mean > Median > Mode, the distribution is positively skewed; if Mode > Median > Mean, it is negatively skewed.

q: The marks obtained by 15 students out of a maximum of 25 in a test are given as 13, 11, 16, 15, 18, 12, 13, 14, 10, 22, 15, 21, 20, 17 and 24. Find the product of the modes of this set of data.
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify frequencies: 13 appears 2 times, 15 appears 2 times.

All other numbers (10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 17, 18, 20, 21, 22, 24) appear only once.

The highest frequency is 2, so the modes are 13 and 15.

Product of modes = 13 × 15 = 195.

∴ The correct answer is 195.

Alternate Method

Given: Data set = {13, 11, 16, 15, 18, 12, 13, 14, 10, 22, 15, 21, 20, 17, 24}

Formula: Mode is the observation(s) with the highest frequency in the data set.



⇒ Arranging the data in ascending order: 10, 11, 12, 13, 13, 14, 15, 15, 16, 17, 18, 20, 21, 22, 24.

⇒ Frequency count:

⇒ 10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 17, 18, 20, 21, 22, 24 → 1 time each.

⇒ 13 → 2 times.

⇒ 15 → 2 times.

⇒ Since 13 and 15 have the highest frequency (2), there are two modes.

⇒ Modes = 13 and 15.

⇒ Product of modes = 13 × 15 = 195.

∴ The correct answer is 195.

Additional Information

Mode of a Dataset

The mode is the value that occurs most frequently in a data set. A set can have one mode (unimodal), two modes (bimodal), or more (multimodal).

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Mean and Median

Mean is the average (sum ÷ count). Median is the middle value when data is arranged in ascending or descending order.

q: A set of data presented in the form of a frequency distribution table with class intervals and their respective frequencies had a mode of 48.5. The lower boundary of the modal class was 46.5; the frequency of the modal class was 34; the frequency of the class interval just preceding the modal class was 32 and the frequency of the class interval just succeeding the modal class was 25. What was the width of the modal class?
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Difference between Mode and Lower limit = (f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) × h

48.5 − 46.5 = (34 − 32) ÷ (2 × 34 − 32 − 25) × h

2 = (2 ÷ 11) × h

h = 11

∴ The correct answer is 11.

Alternate Method

Given:

Mode (Mₒ) = 48.5

Lower boundary of modal class (l) = 46.5

Frequency of modal class (f₁) = 34

Frequency of preceding class (f₀) = 32

Frequency of succeeding class (f₂) = 25

Formula Used:

Mode = l + [ (f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) ] × h



Calculations:

⇒ 48.5 = 46.5 + [ (34 − 32) ÷ (2 × 34 − 32 − 25) ] × h

⇒ 48.5 − 46.5 = [ 2 ÷ (68 − 57) ] × h

⇒ 2 = (2 ÷ 11) × h

⇒ 2 × 11 = 2h

⇒ 22 = 2h

⇒ h = 22 ÷ 2

⇒ h = 11

∴ The correct answer is 11.

Additional Information

Median for Grouped Data

Median = l + [ (N/2 − cf) ÷ f ] × h, where l is lower limit of median class and cf is cumulative frequency of preceding class.

Empirical Relationship

Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean. This formula is used for moderately skewed distributions.

Mean for Grouped Data (Direct Method)

Mean = Σfᵢxᵢ ÷ Σfᵢ, where xᵢ is the class mark (mid-value) of each interval.

q:
The given graph represents the data on the ages of various children.

Study the given graph and answer the question that follows.



What is the difference between the mean and mode of the ages?
solution:
Shortcut Trick

By observing the given bar graph, the data distribution is perfectly symmetrical around the central bar.

For any perfectly symmetrical distribution, the Mean, Median, and Mode are exactly equal.

∴ Mean = Mode

Difference between mean and mode = 0.

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Alternate Method

Given:

From the symmetrical bar graph, we can extract the representative frequencies for the ages:

Ages (x): 8, 9, 10, 11, 12

Number of children (f): 2, 4, 5, 4, 2

Formula Used:

Mean = Σ(fx) ÷ Σf

Mode = Observation with the maximum frequency

Calculations:

⇒ Total sum of ages Σ(fx) = (8 × 2) + (9 × 4) + (10 × 5) + (11 × 4) + (12 × 2)

⇒ Σ(fx) = 16 + 36 + 50 + 44 + 24 = 170

⇒ Total number of children Σf = 2 + 4 + 5 + 4 + 2 = 17

⇒ Mean = 170 ÷ 17 = 10

⇒ The maximum frequency is 5, which corresponds to the age of 10.

⇒ Mode = 10

⇒ Difference = Mean − Mode = 10 − 10 = 0

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Additional Information

Mean

The mean is the average of a dataset, calculated by dividing the sum of all observations by the total number of observations.

Mode

The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set. A set of data may have multiple modes or no mode at all.

Symmetrical Distribution

In a perfectly symmetrical distribution, the Mean, Median, and Mode are all equal and perfectly aligned at the center.

Empirical Relationship

For moderately skewed distributions, the empirical formula is: Mode ≈ 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

q:
Find the median of the following data. (Rounded off to 2 decimal places.)

Class interval 0-5 5-10 10-15 15-20 20-25 25-30 30-35

Frequency 3 5 4 2 7 6 5
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total frequency N = 32 → N/2 = 16.

Cumulative frequency just > 16 is 21, so median class is 20-25.

L = 20, CF = 14, f = 7, h = 5.

Median = 20 + [(16 − 14) ÷ 7] × 5 = 20 + 10/7 ≈ 21.43.

∴ The correct answer is 21.43.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total frequency (N) = 3 + 5 + 4 + 2 + 7 + 6 + 5 = 32

Cumulative frequencies (CF) for classes: 3, 8, 12, 14, 21, 27, 32

Formula Used:

Median = L + [(N/2 − CF) ÷ f] × h

Calculations:

⇒ N/2 = 32 ÷ 2 = 16

⇒ The CF just greater than 16 is 21, which corresponds to the class interval 20-25.

⇒ Lower limit of median class (L) = 20

⇒ CF of preceding class (CF) = 14

⇒ Frequency of median class (f) = 7

⇒ Class size (h) = 5

⇒ Median = 20 + [(16 − 14) ÷ 7] × 5

⇒ Median = 20 + (2 ÷ 7) × 5

⇒ Median = 20 + 10 ÷ 7

⇒ Median = 20 + 1.428...

⇒ Median ≈ 21.43

∴ The correct answer is 21.43.

Additional Information

Mode of Grouped Data

Mode = L + [(f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)] × h, where f₁ is frequency of modal class, f₀ and f₂ are frequencies of preceding and succeeding classes.

Mean of Grouped Data

Direct method formula: Mean = Σfᵢxᵢ ÷ Σfᵢ, where xᵢ represents the class mark (midpoint) of each class interval.

Empirical Relationship

The empirical relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

q:
Find the median of the following data.

Class Interval
0-20
20-40
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Cumulative Frequencies: 9, 25, 49, 64, 68.

Total frequency N = 68 ⇒ N ÷ 2 = 34.

The first cumulative frequency > 34 is 49, hence the median class is 40-60.

Median = l + [(N/2 − CF) ÷ f] × h

Median = 40 + [(34 − 25) ÷ 24] × 20 = 40 + (9 ÷ 24) × 20 = 47.5

∴ The correct answer is 47.5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Class Intervals: 0-20, 20-40, 40-60, 60-80, 80-100

Frequencies: 9, 16, 24, 15, 4

Formula Used:

Median = l + [(N/2 − CF) ÷ f] × h

Where:

l = lower limit of median class

N = total frequency

CF = cumulative frequency of the preceding class

f = frequency of the median class

h = class size

Calculations:

⇒ First, let us construct the cumulative frequency (CF) distribution:

⇒ 0-20: 9

⇒ 20-40: 9 + 16 = 25

⇒ 40-60: 25 + 24 = 49

⇒ 60-80: 49 + 15 = 64

⇒ 80-100: 64 + 4 = 68

⇒ Total frequency (N) = 68 ⇒ N ÷ 2 = 68 ÷ 2 = 34

⇒ The cumulative frequency just greater than 34 is 49, corresponding to the class 40-60.

⇒ Median class = 40-60

⇒ Here, l = 40, CF = 25, f = 24, h = 20

⇒ Median = 40 + [(34 − 25) ÷ 24] × 20

⇒ Median = 40 + (9 ÷ 24) × 20

⇒ Median = 40 + (3 ÷ 8) × 20

⇒ Median = 40 + (60 ÷ 8)

⇒ Median = 40 + 7.5 = 47.5

∴ The correct answer is 47.5.

Additional Information

Mode of Grouped Data

Mode = l + [(f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)] × h, where f₁ is the modal class frequency, f₀ is the preceding class frequency, and f₂ is the succeeding class frequency.

Mean of Grouped Data

Mean = Σ(fᵢxᵢ) ÷ Σfᵢ, where xᵢ represents the class mark or midpoint of each interval, calculated as (lower limit + upper limit) ÷ 2.

Empirical Relationship

Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean. This formula is highly useful to find one of the measures of central tendency when the other two are known for a moderately skewed distribution.

q: The age of some students is given in years as 12, 13, 16, 18,14, 19, 13, 17, 15 and 11. The median age (in years) of the students is:
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Arrange the given data in ascending order: 11, 12, 13, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19.

Since the number of terms n = 10 (even), the median is the simple average of the two middle terms.

Median = Average of the 5th and 6th terms.

Median = (14 + 15) ÷ 2 = 14.5.

∴ The correct answer is 14.5 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

q: A set of n values X₁, X₂, ..., X_n has a standard deviation of 5. The standard deviation of n values X₁ - 7, X₂ - 7, ..., X_n - 7 will be:
solution:
Shortcut Trick

The standard deviation of any given data set is completely independent of the change of origin.

This means adding or subtracting a constant value from all observations does not change the standard deviation, as the overall spread of the data remains the same.

Since each original value is uniformly decreased by 7, the new standard deviation will be exactly equal to the original standard deviation.

∴ The correct answer is 5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Standard deviation of n values X₁, X₂, ..., Xₙ = 5

New values: X₁ − 7, X₂ − 7, ..., Xₙ − 7

Formula Used:

If a new dataset is formed by the linear transformation Yᵢ = aXᵢ + b, then SD(Y) = |a| × SD(X).



Calculations:

⇒ In the new series, each value is generated by shifting the original values by −7.

⇒ Comparing with the general transformation Yᵢ = aXᵢ + b, we get a = 1 and b = −7.

⇒ New Standard Deviation = |1| × Original Standard Deviation

⇒ New Standard Deviation = 1 × 5 = 5

⇒ The subtraction of a constant solely shifts the mean position of the data curve but does not affect the inner dispersion (spread) of the elements.

∴ The correct answer is 5.

Additional Information

Change of Origin (Addition/Subtraction)

Standard deviation and variance are completely independent of the change of origin. Adding or subtracting a constant value to all data points shifts the central mean but perfectly preserves the gaps between the data points.

Change of Scale (Multiplication/Division)

Standard deviation is heavily dependent on the change of scale. If every single observation is identically multiplied or divided by a constant 'k', the new standard deviation inherently becomes |k| times the original standard deviation.

Variance vs Standard Deviation

Variance mathematically behaves as the square of the standard deviation (σ²). Therefore, while the standard deviation formally scales by a factor of |k|, variance fundamentally scales by a factor of k² when values are multiplied by 'k'.

q:
The given table shows the number of people in different age groups. Find the mean age of the given number of people.

Class interval of age (in years)
Number of people (f)

25 - 29
10
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let Assumed Mean (A) = 42 (middle class mark).

Deviations (dᵢ) of class marks from A: −15, −10, −5, 0, +5, +10, +15.

Total deviation = Σfᵢdᵢ = −150 − 120 − 40 + 0 + 75 + 100 + 225 = +90.

Total frequency (Σfᵢ) = 75.

Mean = A + (Σfᵢdᵢ ÷ Σfᵢ) = 42 + (90 ÷ 75) = 42 + 1.2 = 43.2.

∴ The correct answer is 43.2 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Frequencies corresponding to age intervals are provided in the data.

Formula Used:

Mean = Σ(fᵢ × xᵢ) ÷ Σfᵢ

Class mark (xᵢ) = (Lower limit + Upper limit) ÷ 2

Calculation:

⇒ Class marks (xᵢ): 27, 32, 37, 42, 47, 52, 57.

⇒ Frequencies (fᵢ): 10, 12, 8, 5, 15, 10, 15.

⇒ Products (fᵢ × xᵢ): 270, 384, 296, 210, 705, 520, 855.

⇒ Total Frequency (Σfᵢ) = 10 + 12 + 8 + 5 + 15 + 10 + 15 = 75

⇒ Sum of Products (Σfᵢxᵢ) = 270 + 384 + 296 + 210 + 705 + 520 + 855 = 3240

⇒ Mean = 3240 ÷ 75

⇒ Mean = 43.2

∴ The correct answer is 43.2 years.

Additional Information

Class Mark

The mid-point of a class interval is used as the representative value. Class mark = (Lower Limit + Upper Limit) ÷ 2.

Direct Method for Mean

Mean = Σ(fᵢxᵢ) ÷ Σfᵢ, where xᵢ represents the class marks and fᵢ represents the corresponding frequencies.

Assumed Mean Method

Mean = A + (Σfᵢdᵢ ÷ Σfᵢ), where A is the assumed mean and dᵢ = xᵢ − A.

q:
If the marks scored by the students in a class test out of 50 then, Find the Median of the following data:

Marks
Frequency

0-10
5

10-20
8

20-30
6

30-40
6

40-50
5
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total frequency N = 30, so N/2 = 15.

Cumulative frequency crosses 15 in the 20-30 interval (5 + 8 = 13, then 13 + 6 = 19).

Directly apply: Median = Lower limit + [ (N/2 − cf) ÷ f ] × h

Median = 20 + [ (15 − 13) ÷ 6 ] × 10

Median = 20 + 3.33 = 23.33

∴ The correct answer is 23.3 marks.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total frequency (N) = 5 + 8 + 6 + 6 + 5 = 30

Value of N/2 = 30 ÷ 2 = 15

Finding Cumulative Frequencies (cf):

⇒ 0-10: 5

⇒ 10-20: 5 + 8 = 13

⇒ 20-30: 13 + 6 = 19 (This is the median class since cf ≥ 15)

⇒ 30-40: 19 + 6 = 25

⇒ 40-50: 25 + 5 = 30

Formula Used:

Median = L + [ (N/2 − cf) ÷ f ] × h

Where L = Lower limit of median class = 20

cf = Cumulative frequency of preceding class = 13

f = Frequency of median class = 6

h = Class width = 10

Calculation:

⇒ Median = 20 + [ (15 − 13) ÷ 6 ] × 10

⇒ Median = 20 + (2 ÷ 6) × 10

⇒ Median = 20 + 10 ÷ 3

⇒ Median = 20 + 3.33

⇒ Median = 23.33

∴ The correct answer is 23.3 marks.

Additional Information

Mode of Grouped Data

Mode = L + [ (f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2 × f₁ − f₀ − f₂) ] × h, where f₁ is the frequency of the modal class, f₀ is the frequency of the preceding class, and f₂ is the frequency of the succeeding class.

Mean of Grouped Data

Mean = (Σfᵢxᵢ) ÷ Σfᵢ, where xᵢ represents the class marks (midpoints) of the respective intervals.

Empirical Relationship

In a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship between measures of central tendency is: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

q: If the mode of the data set {a, a + 2, a + 4, a + 6, a + 6, a + 6, a + 8} is 26, find a.
solution:
Shortcut Trick

The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set.

By observing the given data set, the term (a + 6) appears 3 times, which is the maximum frequency.

∴ Mode = a + 6

Equating it to the given mode: a + 6 = 26

⇒ a = 20

∴ The correct answer is a = 20.

Alternate Method

Given:

Data set = {a, a + 2, a + 4, a + 6, a + 6, a + 6, a + 8}

Mode = 26

Concept Used:

Mode is the value that appears most frequently in a given set of data points.

Calculations:

⇒ Frequency of a = 1

⇒ Frequency of a + 2 = 1

⇒ Frequency of a + 4 = 1

⇒ Frequency of a + 6 = 3

⇒ Frequency of a + 8 = 1

⇒ Since the term (a + 6) has the highest frequency (3 times), it is the mode of the data set.

⇒ Mode = a + 6

⇒ It is given that the mode is 26.

⇒ a + 6 = 26

⇒ a = 26 − 6 = 20

∴ The correct answer is a = 20.

Additional Information

Mean

The mean is the arithmetic average of the numbers, calculated as the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations.

Median

The median is the exact middle value when a data set is ordered from least to greatest. For an even number of observations, it is the average of the two middle values.

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Bimodal Data

A data set can have more than one mode. If two different values share the highest frequency, the data set is termed bimodal.

q:
The marks obtained by 9 students in a test are: 5, 8, 7, 9, 6, 7, 8, 7, 10.

Determine: (i) Mode of the marks, (ii) Number of students scoring above average.
options: Mode = 7, Number of students scoring above average = 3
Mode = 8, Number of students scoring above average = 4
Mode = 8, Number of students scoring above average = 3
Mode = 7, Number of students scoring above average = 4
solution:
Shortcut Trick

List marks in ascending order: 5, 6, 7, 7, 7, 8, 8, 9, 10.

Mode is the most frequent value ⇒ 7 occurs three times, so Mode = 7.

Average = Sum ÷ Count = 67 ÷ 9 ≈ 7.44.

Marks above 7.44 are 8, 8, 9, 10 ⇒ 4 students.

∴ The correct answer is Mode = 7, 4 students.

Alternate Method

Given:

Marks of 9 students: 5, 8, 7, 9, 6, 7, 8, 7, 10

Formula Used:

Average = Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations



Calculations:

⇒ Sum of marks = 5 + 8 + 7 + 9 + 6 + 7 + 8 + 7 + 10 = 67

⇒ Total number of students = 9

⇒ Average marks = 67 ÷ 9 ≈ 7.44

⇒ To determine the students above average, observe the marks greater than 7.44: 8, 9, 8, 10.

⇒ Number of students scoring above average = 4

⇒ To find the mode, determine the frequency of each distinct mark:

⇒ Mark 5 occurs 1 time

⇒ Mark 6 occurs 1 time

⇒ Mark 7 occurs 3 times

⇒ Mark 8 occurs 2 times

⇒ Mark 9 occurs 1 time

⇒ Mark 10 occurs 1 time

⇒ The mark with the highest frequency is 7.

⇒ Therefore, Mode = 7

∴ The correct answer is Mode = 7, 4 students.

Additional Information

Mean (Average)

The mean is calculated by adding all the values in a dataset and dividing the sum by the total number of observations. It represents the central point of the data.

Median

The median is the exact middle value of a sorted dataset. For an odd number of observations, it is the center value. For an even number, it is the average of the two central values.

Mode

The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a dataset. A set of data may have one mode (unimodal), multiple modes (multimodal), or no mode if all values occur with the same frequency.
